projects.title: Heimdall - Telemetry Character Device Driver
projects.shortDescription: Linux character-device driver in C for Android, with swappable sources behind a versioned seam and a test suite that runs in QEMU and CI.
projects.fullDescription: • Shows up as /dev/telemetry0; streams samples via read, ioctl and copy_to_user. • Three sources (a counter, a timer-fed ring buffer and a replay) swap in behind a versioned source_ops seam. • Four ioctls (version, reset, rate, stats) plus sysfs knobs, guarded by a mutex and an IRQ-safe spinlock. • A Linux CLI drives all of it, and refuses a driver whose ABI doesn't match. • 23 checks run from a cold kernel in QEMU, and fail if the kernel log so much as grumbles. • CI builds on kernels 5.15 and 6.8, cross-compiles for arm64, then loads the module and runs every check.

projects.title: Home Lab Kubernetes Cluster
projects.shortDescription: Enterprise-grade Kubernetes infrastructure with 9 HP Spectre SFF PC nodes, Calico CNI, and GitLab CI/CD.
projects.fullDescription:
• Turned 9 HP small-form-factor PCs into a Kubernetes cluster on Ubuntu, with Calico keeping the networks apart.
• High-availability control plane with load balancing, so losing a node isn't a crisis.
• Packer-built images and a GitLab CI/CD pipeline for zero-downtime deploys.
• Istio for traffic, Prometheus + Grafana for watching it all, and Lens for poking at it.

projects.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection
projects.shortDescription: Architected and benchmarked ML models for fraud detection, improving precision and reducing false positives.
projects.fullDescription:
• Pitted four ML models against each other on fraud detection, across six metrics.
• A feature-selection trick bumped precision by 23% and cut false positives by about 30%.
• Fraud is rare, so I fought the class imbalance with resampling and custom loss functions.
• Published it as first author in IRJMETS, Vol. 4, 2022.
• The lineup: regression, random forest, SVM and nearest neighbour.
• Built toward real-time transaction alerts.
projects.journal: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science (IRJMETS)
projects.citation: Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Credit Card Fraud Detection - Vol 4, 2022
projects.citationContent: Palaspagar, T. (2022). Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Credit Card Fraud Detection. International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science, 4.

projects.title: Advanced Stock Price Prediction System
projects.shortDescription: Developed a stock price prediction system using time series regression, deep learning (LSTM), and Streamlit.
projects.fullDescription:
• Tried to predict the stock market (as one does) with time-series regression and an LSTM.
• FBProphet for the trends and seasonality.
• Wrapped it all in a Streamlit app with live charts and forecasts.
• The LSTM was there to push accuracy past the classic models.

projects.title: Conway's Game of Life in Go and HTMX
projects.shortDescription: Interactive cellular automaton simulation built with Go backend and HTMX frontend, featuring custom router implementation and real-time grid manipulation.
projects.fullDescription: •Why Go and HTMX? Because a famous Netflix employee once said: [link] • Game of Life on a Go backend and an HTMX front end, with not a single JavaScript framework in sight. • Hand-rolled the HTTP router with zero dependencies. • Pre-allocated grid buffers keep the 50x30 world smooth: toggle, step, randomize or wipe it with HTMX partial updates.

projects.title: Smart Solid Waste Management and Composting System
projects.shortDescription: Engineered an Arduino-based IoT prototype for automated organic waste composting.
projects.fullDescription:
• Built a bin that sorts waste and composts it, on Arduino and ESP32.
• Sensors steer the composting conditions automatically.
• Designed the circuits and power management, and logged data to keep improving it.
• Made the national Top 12 at the AICTE Vishwakarma Awards.
• Composting ran 40% more efficiently.
• Went from idea to working prototype in about three months.

projects.title: Fuzzy Logic-Based Fingerprint Recognition System
projects.shortDescription: Advanced biometric authentication system using Fuzzy C-Means clustering and statistical features for fingerprint segmentation and enhancement.
projects.fullDescription:
• Recognized fingerprints with Fuzzy C-Means clustering and statistical features (mean, variance, higher-order moments).
• Sliding-window segmentation cuts the print out of the background noise, and beat K-means at it.
• The full pipeline: segment, enhance, find the minutiae, estimate orientation, classify, match.
• Research under Prof. Surekha Janrao.
• Enhanced prints by diffing the original against its variance and mean images, for cleaner minutiae.
projects.citation: An Application of Fuzzy Logic to Fingerprint Recognition, 2019

projects.title: Bayesian Networks Inference Engine
projects.shortDescription: Command-line probabilistic inference engine implementing Bayesian Networks with conditional probability calculations and evidence-based reasoning.
projects.fullDescription:
• A Bayesian network inference engine in Python, running inference by enumeration.
• Ask it things like P(B=true, G=false | F=false) and get answers to 9 decimal places.
• Learns its probability tables from training data, with epsilon smoothing so zero counts don't break everything.
• Fills in every variable the query leaves out, so the answers are exact.
• Flexible command-line queries with evidence variables.

projects.title: Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithms on Road Networks
projects.shortDescription: Comprehensive analysis and implementation of Prim's and Kruskal's MST algorithms with real-world road network datasets and performance benchmarking.
projects.fullDescription:
• Raced Prim's against Kruskal's on real road maps, from the Maldives (639 nodes) to Tokyo (898,430 nodes).
• Python + NetworkX, with Matplotlib charts of the results.
• The verdict: Prim's wins on dense graphs, Kruskal's on sparse ones.
• In between: Manhattan (4,426 nodes), New York (54,128) and Los Angeles (297,333).
• Timed every run to compare them head to head.

projects.title: Red-Blue Nim Game with Minimax AI
projects.shortDescription: Interactive command-line game implementing Minimax algorithm with alpha-beta pruning for optimal strategy in two-pile marble game.
projects.fullDescription:
• Red-Blue Nim against a Minimax AI that gets as smart as you let it: just set the search depth.
• Its heuristic knows red marbles are worth 2 and blue ones 3, and it always goes for the win.
• Pick the pile sizes, who starts, and how hard it plays, all from the terminal.
• Builds the full game tree and looks ahead before every move.
• Game rules, AI and UI kept cleanly apart.

projects.title: Aquarcade - Underwater Gaming Portal
projects.shortDescription: Responsive web application for underwater-themed arcade gaming zone with dark mode, multi-language support, and billing system.
projects.fullDescription:
• A Subnautica-themed gaming portal, built for IEEE & CSI SIES-GST's Inspect Element 1.0.
• Pick a game, book a slot, and it works out the bill and prints your receipt.
• Dark mode and 3+ languages in plain JavaScript, with a responsive Bootstrap layout on GitHub Pages.
• Search and filters to help players find their game.
• Works in Chrome, Firefox and Safari.

projects.title: Railway e-Ticketing Management System
projects.shortDescription: Full-stack web-based railway reservation system with real-time booking, cancellation, and status tracking capabilities.
projects.fullDescription:
• An online railway reservation system in PHP and MySQL, built to beat the ticket-counter queue.
• Seat allocation, waiting lists that auto-confirm when someone cancels, and PNR numbers.
• Book up to 10 passengers, cancel, or check status; admins manage trains and seats.
• Normalized MySQL tables with live status updates.
• Validates dates, seats and Aadhaar-verified passengers before booking.
